# late_payment

## Functions

A function's effect puts it in one of three parts. A total function answers every input in the ranges it declares. A function checked when it runs has places the checks could not show: the generated code checks the value there, and when it is outside, fails with the kind of the place (`rule` and so on). A function that may not stop recurses.

### Total

#### `claim`

Total: it answers every input in the ranges it declares. Its head writes `total`, and kaname holds it to that.

None when the invoice was paid by the day it fell due.

```kn
fn claim(invoice: Invoice, paid_on: date range >=2026-01-01 <=2029-12-31, reference_rate: rate[step 0.01%] range >=0% <=15%) -> Claim? total
  description "None when the invoice was paid by the day it fell due"
  let due = terms.due(invoiced: invoice.invoiced)
  let late = paid_on - due
  if late >= 1
    let c = charges(debt: invoice.amount, days_late: late, reference_rate: reference_rate)
    Claim { due: due, days_late: late, compensation: c.compensation, interest: c.interest }
  else
    none
```
